comment: The edge worker's authorized-delivery record, as one payload both languages check against.
The worker writes this record in TypeScript (src/edge/src/log.ts) and the ramp-ledger
renderer parses it in Go (src/broker/cmd/ramp-ledger/edgelog.go). Nothing in either
language's own tests makes them agree: renaming a key in the worker AND its test together
leaves both suites green while the Go side silently stops reading the field.
That drift does not surface as a missing record. CloudWatch matches the digest as a plain
substring of the raw line, so a renamed key is still found; Go then ignores the unknown key
and the delivered-URL assertion fails, which reads as tampering rather than as a rename.
So this file is the third party neither side's tests control. The TypeScript suite asserts
that a record the worker ACTUALLY EMITTED carries every key listed here; the Go suite parses
the payload below and asserts every value. Adding a field to the record means adding it here,
in the same change, or one of the two fails.
This is a checked-in fixture, never generated by a test run: `make test-fast` runs the Go
suite before the edge suite, so a file written by the TypeScript tests would not exist yet
when Go looked for it on a clean checkout.

optional_keys.kid: absent when the signed URL carried no key id
optional_keys.agent_id: absent when the signed URL named no agent
optional_keys.origin_status: absent on the runtimes where the worker never sees an origin response

load_bearing_keys.comment: Without either of these the record cannot be joined or described, so the Go parser refuses it rather than rendering blanks.
